thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated OOM/CUDA error rate on inference-prod-us-west-1 cluster. Symptoms: node flaps (3 nodes), repeated CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY, paged-allocator OOMs. See alert: https://alerts.redwood.internal/1975502468 :warning:

maria: ack. I'm oncall SRE for the shift. pinging @eng-runtime @eng-oncall. collecting logs now.

kevin: on it. which node IDs? any obvious pattern (model, seq len, route)?

maria: nodes: gpu-node-14, gpu-node-17, gpu-node-21. Affected routes: /v1/generate (mixed small+long seqs). Noticing slow memory creep before hard OOM.

anita: quick note — GPU util is fine, it's GPU memory fragmentation and paging. We've seen similar slow-creep fragmentation before.

maria: pasting recent runtime excerpt:

```
2026-03-15T02:34:12Z runtime ERROR paged-allocator alloc failed size=2097152 err=CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
2026-03-15T02:34:12Z runtime WARN kvcache fragmented_pages=1245 total_pages=4096 free_pages=28
2026-03-15T02:34:12Z runtime ERROR attention-paged::page_fault: failed to materialize kv page id=0x7f12c3
```

ryan: that log pattern + fragmented_pages high = likely paged-attention allocator fragmentation + eviction not keeping up. Could be a defrag race where partial frees leave unusable holes.

kevin: can we confirm per-process CUDA OOM traces? run on node: `kubectl -n infra exec -it pod/runtime-<node> -- journalctl -u runtime -n 200` and `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory --format=csv`

maria: running checks now. output (trimmed):

```
-- runtime journal --
E 2026-03-15T02:33:52 Failed allocation: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
E 2026-03-15T02:34:12 paged-alloc: fragmentation threshold exceeded
-- nvidia-smi --
pid  4321, used 10231 MiB
pid  4388, used 10312 MiB
pid  4410, used 2012 MiB
```

eli: support note — initial customer impact: 4 customers seeing sporadic 5xx in US-WEST, ~1-3% error rate on /v1/generate. No billing impact reported yet. Lane: high-reliability customers flagged.

anita: recommendation: temporarily divert traffic for heavy-seq customers to dedicated-cluster while we mitigate.

kevin: mitigation plan attempt 1 (live):
- reduce per-pod concurrency to 2 on affected deployments
- increase kvcache eviction aggressiveness (ENV KVCACHE_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.6 -> 0.4)
- schedule rolling restart of affected pods with 30s gap

maria: executing concurrency change now: `kubectl -n inference set resources deployment runtime-worker --replicas=20` and patch configmap concurrency -> 2.

deploy-bot: Patch applied to deployments: runtime-worker (namespace inference). Restarting pods 4 at a time.

anita: cordoned gpu-node-17 and drained gracefully to reduce flapping risk.

ryan: while that's running, please run this quick LRU eviction override on the running pod(s):
```
echo "evict_now" > /proc/runtime/kvcache/control
```
That will force immediate eviction of cold prefixes and return free pages. Use with caution.

maria: ran evict_now on gpu-node-14 pod. kvcache fragmented_pages dropped from 1245 -> 180 within 45s. error rate dropped from 2.8% -> 0.6%.

kevin: good signal. hypothesis: there is a slow memory leak tied to paged-attention defrag when eviction fails under certain seq-length mixes. eviction worker either stalls or loses reference accounting.

ryan: agreed. short-term: keep aggressive evictions + reduced concurrency + route diversion. Medium-term: need a runtime patch to fix defrag race and add stronger metrics + self-evicting background job.

maria: customer update drafted: "We observed elevated memory fragmentation leading to OOMs on a subset of inference hosts in US-WEST. We mitigated by diverting heavy-sequence traffic, forcing KV cache eviction, and rolling pods — service restored to nominal error rates. Root cause under investigation; ETA for fix TBD." @eli will send.

eli: sent customer comms to flagged list. No escalations yet. customers thanked us for rapid mitigation.

anita: creating a follow-up incident ticket and linking to this thread. tagging @eng-runtime for a postmortem.

kevin: planned hotfix: bump eviction frequency, add a guard that prevents defrag concurrent-free-path race, and add a metric for fragmented_pages delta/hour. Will open PR and request urgent review. If OK, we can hotpatch a build to staging for verification.

ryan: QA checklist for hotpatch: reproduce with synthetic long-short seq traffic, verify fragmented_pages stabilizes under sustained load, confirm no perf regression with quantized kernels.

maria: immediate mitigation checklist (done/in-progress):
- [x] divert heavy-seq traffic to dedicated cluster (anita)
- [x] run manual evict_now on affected pods (maria)
- [x] reduce per-pod concurrency (maria)
- [x] rolling restart of affected pods (deploy-bot)
- [x] node cordon/drain on flapping nodes (anita)
- [ ] deploy runtime hotfix (eng-runtime -> next 24h)
- [ ] postmortem & customer RCA (assigned kevin/ryan)
kevin: I'll open the hotfix PR now and link the test harness. Expecting initial PR in ~2h.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated — error rate for /v1/generate down to 0.4% (pre-incident baseline ~0.1%). Monitoring for 1h. Incident state -> MONITORING.

maria: handing off to overnight oncall @eng-oncall. Summary: paged-attn fragmentation causing slow memory creep -> OOMs; mitigations applied; runtime team working on hotfix; follow-up ticket created.

anita: noted. I'll add runbook steps for forced evict and when to cordon nodes.

kevin: thanks all. I'll be available for reviews. please ping me if we see >1% error rate again. :thumbsup:

ryan: adding a unit test to prevent regressions in defrag path.

maria: closing thread for now — will reopen if we see reoccur. :white_check_mark:
